title: 3rd Stopping Place 4th Truth The Seal Of Unity In The Manifestation Of The Compassionate And The Provider

questions.question: What small food is used as the main example in this passage?
questions.answer: An apple.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can make that fruit and give it to people as real food?
questions.answer: Allah, the Creator of everything.

questions.question: What big things in the world are mentioned to show this great power?
questions.answer: The seasons, day and night, and the earth moving.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect one apple to those very big things?
questions.answer: Because bringing one fruit needs control over the whole world around it.

questions.question: What does the passage say is found on one apple and also on other fruits, plants, and animals?
questions.answer: Signs of wisdom, mercy, and one Maker.

questions.question: If the same special signs are on many living things, what does that help us understand?
questions.answer: They all come from the same Creator.

questions.question: How is the earth described in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: Like its garden.

questions.question: How is the whole universe described in relation to the apple?
questions.answer: Like a great tree or factory for it.

questions.question: What do spring and summer do for the fruit in the passage?
questions.answer: They are the times when it grows and ripens.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: Even one fruit shows Allah’s oneness and power over all creation.

questions.question: What gift to a person does the passage talk about first?
questions.answer: Giving a person an apple for food.

questions.question: Is that gift shown as a small, easy thing or as something needing great power?
questions.answer: It is shown as needing great power.

questions.question: What moving parts of the world are named in the passage?
questions.answer: The seasons, the days, the nights, and the earth.

questions.question: Why are people on earth called needy guests in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they need food given to them.

questions.question: What idea does the passage teach by saying fruits of different times are brought close to people?
questions.answer: Allah arranges the world so people can receive their food.

questions.question: What does the passage say about apples and other fruits being alike in an important way?
questions.answer: They all carry the same signs from their Maker.

questions.question: What does that sameness tell us about who made them?
questions.answer: One Lord made them all.

questions.question: Besides fruits, what other living things are named with them?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: Why must the Maker of an apple also be the Maker of the earth?
questions.answer: Because the apple depends on the earth and the whole system around it.

questions.question: What does every fruit become, according to the last sentence?
questions.answer: A sign that points to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What is one apple called for a human being in this passage?
questions.answer: Real provision or sustenance.

questions.question: What does the passage say must happen in the world for that provision to reach people?
questions.answer: The world must be run in an ordered way.

questions.question: Which repeating changes are mentioned as part of that order?
questions.answer: The changing seasons and the turning of day and night.

questions.question: What picture is used for the earth in motion?
questions.answer: A ship carrying loads.

questions.question: What is being carried to people, like on that ship?
questions.answer: The fruits of different seasons.

questions.question: What kind of marks on the apple are talked about?
questions.answer: Marks of wisdom, mercy, and a Creator.

questions.question: Are those marks only on one apple?
questions.answer: No, they are on all apples and many other living things too.

questions.question: If many things have the same marks, what can we infer?
questions.answer: They were made by the same One.

questions.question: What family-like words are used to show the apple belongs with other created things?
questions.answer: It is shown as being with its kindred and fellow creatures.

questions.question: In simple words, what does the passage want us to notice when we see fruit?
questions.answer: Fruit helps us remember Allah made everything.

questions.question: What does the passage use to teach about Allah’s oneness: a mountain, an apple, or a river?
questions.answer: An apple.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the One who gives that fruit as food?
questions.answer: He controls the whole world.

questions.question: Name two large patterns in nature mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: The seasons and the cycle of day and night.

questions.question: How does the passage show that one fruit is connected to the whole earth?
questions.answer: It says the fruit needs the earth and its order to be brought to people.

questions.question: What does the passage say appears on the outside of the apple?
questions.answer: Signs that show wise and merciful making.

questions.question: Are similar signs found only on fruit?
questions.answer: No, they are also found on plants and animals.

questions.question: What does this repeated pattern help prove?
questions.answer: That there is one Creator of all.

questions.question: What place is compared to a garden for the apple?
questions.answer: The earth.

questions.question: What place is compared to a workshop for the apple?
questions.answer: The seasons.

questions.question: What is a fruit called in the last part of the passage because it points to one Creator?
questions.answer: A seal or sign of unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about making even one apple?
questions.answer: It can only be done by the Lord with great power.

questions.question: What world-sized jobs are linked to making that one fruit?
questions.answer: Running time, moving the earth, and bringing seasons.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention waiting people on earth?
questions.answer: To show people need the food Allah sends.

questions.question: What is special about the signs found on an apple?
questions.answer: The same kind of signs are found on many created things.

questions.question: What are some of those other created things?
questions.answer: Other fruits, plants, and animals.

questions.question: What conclusion should we make from the same signs being on all of them?
questions.answer: One Maker created them all.

questions.question: What is the whole world called for the apple?
questions.answer: Its garden.

questions.question: What is the whole cosmos called for the apple?
questions.answer: Its great tree or factory.

questions.question: Which seasons are named as the fruit’s growing time?
questions.answer: Spring and summer.

questions.question: What does every fruit show about Allah?
questions.answer: It shows His oneness.

questions.question: Which single piece of food is used to teach a big lesson in this passage?
questions.answer: One apple.

questions.question: What lesson does that apple teach about its Maker?
questions.answer: Its Maker is the Lord of everything.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Lord does with nights and days?
questions.answer: He makes them follow one another.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Lord does with the earth?
questions.answer: He makes it move like a loaded ship.

questions.question: Why is that movement important in the passage?
questions.answer: It helps bring seasonal foods to people.

questions.question: What word from the passage means a sign that points to one Maker?
questions.answer: A seal.

questions.question: Is each fruit just food, or is it also a sign?
questions.answer: It is also a sign.

questions.question: What other things besides fruits carry signs from the same Maker?
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: Why can’t the apple have a separate maker from the rest of creation?
questions.answer: Because it belongs to the same world and depends on the same order.

questions.question: What should a Muslim child remember after reading this passage?
questions.answer: Even one fruit is a gift from Allah and a sign of His oneness.
